quotes.text: There is a natural, logical division in terms of the two collections – each of the 1962-1966 and 1967-1970 epochs cohere remarkably well in terms of telling a story of The Beatles becoming The Beatles in the first, and what they decided to do once they became The Beatles in the second.

There is a breathtaking rate of improvement in terms of song quality, lyrics, musicianship, and messaging from beginning to end on the Red album, although even so every single song on it is outstanding. Just watching them grow to reach their full potential is a remarkable experience.

The film culminates with their legendary rooftop concert, playing music that no one had heard before, not as head-shaking mop-tops, but as four pros, presenting sophisticated, complex pop music, and having a ball.
Cott examines the seeds of Lennon's "Strawberry Fields" (originally titled "It's Not Too Bad") and how it was recorded in 26 takes over 45 hours during a four-week period.
